text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average resumed its climb Tuesday, rising more than 90 points on the back of strong gains in a handful of stocks and a steady bond market.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow was up 90.30 points at 6,750.51, rebounding from Monday's 44-point selloff.
In the broader market, advances issues led declines by a small margin on active trading of more than 260 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

The main movers in the 30-stock Dow index were General Electric Co., up 2-1/2 at 106-3/4, Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co., up 3-3/8 at 86-5/8, Procter & Gamble Co., up 2-3/4 at 125-3/4 and Merck & Co., up 1-3/4 at 88-1/4.
In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury bond was up 5/32, lowering its yield to 7.08 percent from Monday's close of 7.09 percent. The price and yield move in opposite directions.
Ricky Harrington, technical analyst at Interstate/Johnson Lane, said that while blue chips were strong, the secondary market was weak.
"This market is sick. Technically, it looks very negative," he said.

"There is a weak secondary market below the strong blue chip market. The average investors looking at the Dow is getting the wrong impression because these rallies are driven by index funds and programmes," Harrington said. "The secondaries aren't going anywhere."
The Nasdaq Composite index steadied slightly above the day's low but still held a loss of 1.23 points at 1,202.72.

Among actively traded Nasdaq issues, Cisco Systems Inc., was down 11/32 at 46-5/8, 3Com Corp. was down 1-1/8 at 25-1/4, Microsoft Corp. was up 1-3/4 at 109-3/8, Intel Corp. was up 1-3/8 at 139-3/4. Netscape Communications Corp. fell 2 to 24-3/8.

"The market always goes to extremes, particularly when you have a group like the techs which is owned heavily by money managers who tend to follow the herd," said Alfred Goldman, analyst at A.G. Edwards & Sons.

"But the techs are one of the groups of this decade," he said. "Buy them when they show signs of basing, after a period of backing and filling. Wherever they are going, they haven't gotten there yet ... What you are seeing now is aggressive selling and reluctant buying."
